task: E9: does dropping the saturated scenarios move LikePhys D1? (zero GPU)
threads_why: The probe is not bit-reproducible across BLAS thread counts (first measured in E16). All E9 numbers use 4 so they are comparable to E8's delivered cells; the all-clips D1 here is 32.898%, which is exactly E8's LikePhys L16/t=600 value, and that match is the self-check.

saturation_definition.rule: AUC >= 1 - 1e-9 on BOTH trained and random
saturation_definition.why_strict: AUC = 1.0 is the ceiling of a bounded rank statistic (PROTOCOL_VALIDITY D3/D6). A looser delta would call 0.995 'saturated', which is strong signal rather than a statistical ceiling, and only the latter justifies exclusion.

selfcheck.rule: all-clips pooled D1 must equal E8's delivered LikePhys L16/t=600 value
selfcheck.note: matches to the displayed precision; the pooled arm reuses e8_analyse.probe

why_two_aggregates: Pooled D1 recomputes AUC over all clips (E8's convention); the per-scenario mean averages 12 separate D1 values (what 'saturated scenarios drag the mean down' literally describes). They are different quantities and E9_PREREG.md §3 forbids promoting either to 'the' main result.

known_discrepancies.saturated_count: 2 at L16/t=600, not the 5 claimed in NEXT_STEPS_AND_DIVISION.md §1. The 5/12 in EXPERIMENTS.md §5.6 (D3) was measured on L14/t=400, whose features are NOT cached on this node (load_X returns None), so it can neither be confirmed nor refuted here. Registered, not overwritten.
known_discrepancies.shadow_camera: AUC_real 0.3662 < 0.5 — the network ranked physics-violating clips ABOVE legal ones. D1 is undefined (negative denominator), not small. Excluded from both per-scenario means so the two sides average over the same scenario set.
